topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's focus on cancer evolution and outlines the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how mutations and chromatin changes confer selective advantages that drive clonal expansion in pre-malignant tissues.

topics.label: The cancer stem cell model and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate whether malignancies originate from tissue stem cells or committed progenitors using evidence from leukemias and intestinal crypt models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory drivers of tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how external environmental exposures and local stromal signals foster permissive conditions for malignant outgrowth and maintenance.

topics.label: Experimental technologies for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details sequencing and spatial omics technologies used to resolve tumor architecture and evolutionary timelines.

topics.label: Multi-factorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how genetic, epigenetic, cell-of-origin, and microenvironmental factors interact to drive malignant transformation and tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
